::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Solving a Linear System with 5 Equations and 6 Variables](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/4958095/solving-a-linear-system-with-5-equations-and-6-variables), asked by [Someone](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/1264858/someone) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2024-08-13; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> Variables $a,b,c,d,e,f$ are real numbers such that: 
> $$\begin{align} &a+b+c+d+e+f=0 \\ &a+2b+3c+4d+2e+2f=0 \\ &a+3b+6c+9d +4e +6f=0 \\ &a+4b+10c+16d+8e+24f=0 \\ &a+5b+15c +25d+16e+120f=42\end{align}$$
>
> then the question is to find the sum of digits of $a+6b+21c+36d+32e+720f$.
>
> My attempt: I tried subtracting, and solving using matrix, but can't solve further. Any hints would help a lot. To elaborate, from subtracting equation $5$ and $4$, $4$ and $3$, $3$ and $2$, and $4-3-2$ and  $3-2-1$ , I was able to reduce: $a=28f$, $e=\frac{13f}5$, $a= \frac{84e}{13}$ but cannot solve further.
:::

Although the number of equations and variables makes the calculation by hand rather tedious, this is a straightforward application of Gaussian elimination. 

One shortcut would be to add one more variable, let's call it $g$, and one more equation:
$$a+6b+21c+36d+32e+720f-g = 0$$
There is one free variable, but once you solve the system, you will see $g$ does not depend on it.
